sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Visual Web Template and Low-Code Web Application Builder

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980), as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Business Corporations Act (Alberta), R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, s. 114.1 (register of individuals with significant control); Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, as amended; Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), as amended, ss. 233.3 and 233.4; FINTRAC guidance and PCMLTFA regulations; applicable Alberta corporate registry rules for disclosure of individuals with significant control.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the ultimate beneficial owner's valid passport or national identity document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or identity document issuing authority of the UBO's country of citizenship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification followed by Hague Apostille if the issuing country is a Hague Convention member; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Canadian embassy or consulate having jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Certificate of Status showing the corporate incorporator, directors, and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or corporate registry of the jurisdiction in which the corporate incorporator or parent entity is domiciled
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the document's country of origin; if not a Hague member, Consular Legalization by the Canadian consular office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the foreign corporate incorporator authorizing the incorporation of the Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation and appointment of founding directors and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign corporate incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certificate of authenticity from the corporate secretary followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, and each individual with significant control against the Government of Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, and applicable targeted sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, the United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2, and the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 1999, c. 18. PEP determination must follow FINTRAC's Politically Exposed Persons and Heads of International Organizations guidance, with enhanced due diligence triggered by PEP status, sanctions list matches, or opaque multi-layered ownership structures.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry operated by Service Alberta; NUANS name search and corporate registration filings are accepted online through authorized Corporate Registry Access agents and the official portal at https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) may be in English, French, or both. Names must use Roman alphabet characters, Arabic numerals, and permitted punctuation; names originating in other scripts must be transliterated into Roman characters for the NUANS search and registry record. An Alberta unlimited liability corporation must end its legal name with an approved unlimited liability designator such as 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', 'Société à responsabilité illimitée', or 'S.A.R.I.'; limited-liability designators such as 'Ltd.' or 'Inc.' are not permitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An Alberta NUANS name search report / name reservation is valid for 90 days and cannot be extended; if incorporation is not completed within that period, a fresh NUANS search and reservation fee are required. If the Director of Corporate Registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with Service Alberta within 30 days, attaching the clean NUANS report and any consent letter from the holder of an existing confusingly similar name; if the Director maintains the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Business Corporations Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9 within the applicable statutory appeal period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally acceptable. The Alberta ULC must maintain a registered office in Alberta at a real physical street address; a post office box is prohibited. For this low-risk no-code SaaS business, a virtual office package providing a physical Alberta street address, mail forwarding, and reliable access to corporate records will satisfy the ABCA registered office requirement, provided the records are readily producible and the arrangement is not used to evade CRA, FINTRAC, or Alberta corporate registry substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 2-5% annual likelihood) for a digital no-code website-builder with a standard low AML risk profile; CRA compliance activity is ordinarily initiated by correspondence or book review rather than unannounced on-site inspection. The ULC's unlimited liability structure and potential pass-through-oriented shareholding with non-resident UBOs may elevate the likelihood of a CRA substance questionnaire or records inspection at the registered office or accountant's office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS corporate name search report for Alberta ULC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Service Alberta / authorized NUANS service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Service Alberta fee schedule; approximate CAD 45 converted to USD
Statutory tariff; approximate CAD 25 name reservation fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Articles of Incorporation filing fee for Alberta unlimited liability corporation including initial individual-with-significant-control register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff; approximate CAD 100 incorporation filing fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation of articles, unanimous shareholder agreement where required, minute book, ISC/UBO register, consents, and incorporation filing packages
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Alberta corporate law firm / certified corporate services agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a single-UBO Alberta ULC; range approximately CAD 800-1,200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization of foreign UBO and corporate incorporator documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in country of document origin plus competent apostille authority or Canadian consular office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; actual cost depends on the competent authority and number of documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and corporate records address service, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta registered agent / virtual office provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; approximately CAD 150-300 per year for a physical Alberta street address with mail forwarding

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening compliance file, including sanctions database searches and UBO verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance consultant or corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a low-risk, non-PEP UBO verification using consolidated UN, Canadian, and OFAC sanctions sources

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c. B-9, including section 2 on incorporation, sections 6-8 on articles, certificate and corporate name, and applicable provisions governing registered offices, directors, officers, share issuance, corporate records and annual returns.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, administered by Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction through authorized registry agents.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation, together with the Alberta Corporate Registry incorporation application, Notice of Address and Notice of Directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued for legally permitted consideration. No statutory escrow account is required, although subscription funds may be placed in escrow by contract, financing terms or counsel instructions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation accept and record the subscription for the issued shares described in the Articles of Incorporation and issue those shares upon receipt of the agreed consideration. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office and records office stated in the incorporation filings are adopted as the Corporation's offices. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the following persons are appointed as directors and officers, effective immediately: [names and offices]. The officers are authorized to open bank and payment accounts, execute routine contracts, maintain statutory records, and complete all filings required by Alberta Corporate Registry and applicable tax authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm ULC Structure, Name and Director Eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry name search and authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the proposed name complies with the Alberta Business Corporations Act and obtain a NUANS or Alberta name search where required. Confirm the ULC liability wording in the articles, ownership structure, registered office, records office and director composition. If the Corporation has fewer than four directors, appoint at least one resident Canadian director; otherwise, ensure the statutory resident-director percentage is satisfied.
required_dossiers: Name search or NUANS report, where required
Registered office and records office details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace a confusing or unavailable name, correct director eligibility defects, and resubmit the registry-agent application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles and Corporate Registry Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized registry agent or approved electronic filing channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Articles of Incorporation, registered-office information, records-office information and Notice of Directors. Specify the share structure and any ULC provisions in the articles. Pay the applicable government fee and registry-agent service fee. Alberta generally does not require notarization for ordinary incorporation filings; notarized or certified copies should be supplied only if specifically requested or required for foreign use.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to registry queries through the filing agent, amend defective articles or notices, correct fee or identity discrepancies, and resubmit before the application is abandoned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate and Establish Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry and the Corporation's registered records office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, filed articles and registry confirmation. Prepare the minute book, share register, securities ledger, director and officer register, beneficial ownership register and corporate resolutions. Issue shares only after the subscription consideration is received or legally documented. Retain records at the records office and update the registry promptly after changes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct missing records by resolution, obtain replacement registry documents, and file amended notices where corporate particulars are inaccurate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors, financial institution and payment-service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational board meeting or execute written resolutions. Approve share subscriptions, adopt the registered office, appoint officers, authorize bank and payment accounts, approve accounting policies, delegate signing authority and adopt conflicts, privacy and information-security procedures appropriate to the software business. Complete identity verification and beneficial-owner disclosures required by financial institutions, Stripe and Paddle.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide missing corporate, ownership or identification documents; replace rejected signatories; and re-submit account-opening or payment-onboarding materials.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Payroll and Annual Compliance Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration, and Employment Standards or Workers' Compensation authorities where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a CRA Business Number and register applicable program accounts, including corporate income tax, GST/HST and payroll. Assess Alberta corporate tax filing obligations and the ULC's tax classification in each relevant foreign jurisdiction. Register for workers' compensation and payroll remittances when employees or covered workers are engaged. File the Alberta annual return and maintain corporate records by the statutory deadline.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct CRA or provincial registration data, provide requested ownership or tax-residency evidence, and file overdue returns with applicable penalties and interest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial licensing board is ordinarily required for a software and no-code web application business. Alberta Corporate Registry remains the corporate authority; the applicable municipality may require a local business licence or home-based business approval.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial manufacturing or industrial operating permit. Obtain a municipal business licence, development permit or home-occupation approval if required by the municipality and premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from a project-specific EIA for office-based software development and cloud-delivered services; environmental approvals may apply if the business undertakes construction, industrial operations, regulated releases or waste-generating physical activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine wastewater, VOC or industrial-emissions threshold ordinarily applies to a software office. Any discharge, hazardous-material storage, regulated waste or emission must comply with Alberta's Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, applicable regulations, approvals and municipal requirements. Electronic and battery waste must be handled through lawful recycling or waste contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For ordinary office operations, obtain any municipal occupancy, development or fire inspection approval required for the premises. Fire-code compliance, emergency procedures and building-load approvals are handled by the municipality or local fire authority. Alberta Occupational Health and Safety requirements apply to employees and contractors; specialized structural, electrical or industrial clearances are required only if the premises or operations create the relevant risk.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal income tax and GST/HST; Alberta Ministry of Finance / Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration as provincial collection agent under the Tax Collection Agreement; registration portal: CRA Business Registration Online and CRA My Business Account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an Alberta ULC: (1) incorporate the ULC under the Alberta Business Corporations Act through the Alberta Corporate Registry and obtain the Alberta corporation number; (2) apply for a federal Business Number (BN) using CRA Form RC1 or through CRA Business Registration Online; the BN is the national income tax identification number; (3) activate the required CRA program accounts: RC for corporate income tax, RT for GST/HST, and RP/RM for payroll and import/export where applicable; (4) for foreign stakeholders, no separate Canadian TIN is required for the ULC itself, though a non-resident carrying on business in Canada may require a separate CRA non-resident account; (5) Alberta corporate income tax registration is administered through the same CRA BN and does not require a separate Alberta tax identification number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a domestic check-the-box election. An Alberta ULC is a corporation under the Income Tax Act and is taxed at the entity level for Canadian federal and Alberta corporate income tax. The pass-through eligibility arises only under foreign classification regimes, principally the U.S. check-the-box election: an eligible ULC may file IRS Form 8832 to be classified as a disregarded entity or partnership for U.S. federal tax purposes. This foreign election does not alter Canadian tax classification and does not create Canadian tax transparency. For GST/HST purposes, a registrant may elect filing frequencies and certain simplified procedures, but no election exists to treat the ULC as an unregistered/nontaxable entity for GST/HST while carrying on a taxable commercial activity in Canada.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax), a federal value-added tax; Alberta does not impose a provincial retail sales tax or provincial HST component, so the applicable rate in Alberta is the 5% federal GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies made in Canada over the preceding four calendar quarters; non-resident persons making specified digital supplies to Canadian recipients are subject to the same CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold and, if exceeded, must register for the simplified GST/HST digital services regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose a mandatory real-time electronic invoicing or fiscal clearance system. There is no government digital stamping or pre-clearance API for invoices. CRA registrants must retain books and records in a readable electronic format, and most GST/HST registrants must file returns and remit electronically through GST/HST NETFILE and CRA My Payment. Voluntary electronic invoicing may be exchanged through Peppol BIS, EDI, or PDF, but no CRA clearance is required before issuing invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act generally applies to supplies of goods exported from Canada and to supplies of services and intangible personal property made to non-residents where the supply is not for use or consumption in Canada and is not connected to Canadian real property or tangible personal property. For a no-code website builder or low-code SaaS platform, export zero-rating is available when the recipient is a non-resident, the digital service is delivered and consumed outside Canada, and the supplier retains contemporaneous evidence of the non-resident status, place of benefit, and payment from outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA EDI or Form B13A) for physical exports; for digital no-code services, the equivalent export evidence is a signed service contract with a non-resident recipient.
Bill of Lading/air waybill/carrier proof for physical exports; for digital services, technical delivery logs, IP geolocation data, and server/hosting records demonstrating supply outside Canada.
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice (SWIFT MT103, letter of credit, or comparable proof) confirming receipt of export proceeds from the non-resident customer.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess GST/HST beyond the normal four-year limitation period where a registrant has made a misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default, or fraud, and may recover GST at 5% plus interest on any export zero-rating claim that lacks sufficient documentary substantiation. False or grossly negligent export claims attract penalties under the Excise Tax Act, including a penalty equal to 25% of the net tax understated or refund overstated, and may be subject to criminal prosecution for tax evasion. CRA also requires repayment of any input tax credits linked to improperly zero-rated supplies and may issue a formal demand or penalty for failure to provide export evidence during an audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), exercising monetary authority; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) regulates banking; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) enforces AML/KYC; the Department of Finance administers currency exchange policy; the Investment Review Division of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) enforces foreign investment review.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully floating exchange-rate regime with no general exchange-control legislation; the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible into CAD. Profit remittance via dividend, interest, royalty, or management fee is unrestricted, but non-resident withholdings under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (25% standard, reduced to 5% for dividends and 15% for interest/royalties under the Canada-US Tax Treaty for a qualifying US corporate shareholder) apply. A ULC is treated as a Canadian resident corporation and must file T106 and T1134 related-party and foreign-asset information returns where applicable; no exchange-control approval or surrender requirement applies to in-bound equity injections or out-bound operational disbursements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation for Canadian export receipts. A no-code website builder's subscription and licensing revenue may be retained in USD or other foreign currency in any eligible foreign-currency bank account; however, for Canadian tax purposes, the ULC's tax-year revenue, expenses, and paid-up capital must be translated into CAD using an auditable exchange-rate convention (Bank of Canada daily rate or functional-currency election under section 261 of the Income Tax Act). Foreign-exchange gains/losses are taxable/deductible on an accrual or realization basis depending on the hedging designation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, with caution. Unregulated offshore digital EMI accounts cannot act as a primary settlement bank because Payments Canada membership is required for direct clearing in CAD; however, licensed Canadian payment service providers (e.g., Wise Platform, Corpay, Ebury, and Stripe Treasury) are feasible for USD/CAD payables, sub-account treasury, and payout automation once the ULC has a Tier 1 funding account. Such fintechs are now required to register with FINTRAC and, if providing retail payment services, obtain a licence under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA); they remain acceptable as overlay rails but not as the KYC/beneficial-ownership anchor for the Alberta ULC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-branch interview at a Canadian Tier 1 bank is the de facto industry standard for a newly incorporated Alberta ULC with non-resident shareholders and directors. A Canadian-resident director or authorized Canadian-resident signing officer is strongly preferred; under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA), a majority of the ULC's directors must be resident Canadians unless a valid exception applies, so at least one resident director can satisfy the interview. Remote video identity verification is possible only for existing international clients of the bank's cross-border desk; for a first-time ULC, one director must attend in person at a Calgary, Edmonton, Vancouver, or Toronto branch with original corporate documents, or the ULC must appoint a Canadian registered agent/corporate signatory co-signing the mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC's unlimited liability structure: banks may flag the unlimited-liability share class as an abnormal vehicle inconsistent with a simple SaaS treasury, triggering enhanced due diligence on the parent-guarantee chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the ULC's Certificate of Incorporation (or Articles of Amendment/Continuance), Unanimous Shareholder Agreement, parent-company resolution, a Canadian legal opinion confirming the ULC's purpose and unlimited-liability mechanics, and the parent's most recent audited financial statements to evidence that the unlimited liability is a tax-election artifact rather than a credit-risk concealment structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: US check-the-box pass-through election: the Canadian ULC may be disregarded for US federal tax purposes while still being a Canadian corporation for Canadian tax; this cross-border tax mismatch is frequently misread as a skimming or intercompany-pricing vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide IRS Form 8832 election copy, Canadian counsel tax-opinion confirming the ULC's ownership chain, transfer-pricing documentation for intercompany SaaS licensing fees, and a written treasury mandate from the US parent authorizing the Canadian bank account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial ownership: a wholly US-owned ULC with non-resident directors raises UBO, source-of-wealth, and sanctions-scope questions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarized passports of all UBOs (natural persons), corporate registry extracts for the parent chain, a UBO declaration per FINTRAC Schedule A, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence tied to Stripe/Paddle SaaS revenue, and proof that no UBO is a politically exposed person or sanctioned entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry-specific conduct risk: a no-code website builder can be misused for phishing, counterfeit storefronts, or malicious code injection, which may place tech-forward banks on heightened acceptance-scrutiny triggers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a compliance pack comprising the company's acceptable-use policy, platform-abuse takedown procedure, customer KYC flow, DMCA/CCPA compliance attestation, and a statement of transaction velocity (expected MRR, card volumes routed through Stripe/Paddle) to demonstrate that banking activity is recurring, contract-based, and low-volatility.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The US parent should inject equity via a SWIFT MT103 wire to the ULC's Tier 1 CAD currency account using the remitter's stated purpose code 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY INJECTION' (IMF BPM6 counterpart for direct investment; Statistics Canada foreign-direct-investment program code). The bank will require a board resolution of the ULC issuing unlimited-liability shares to the US parent, a share subscription record, and a statement that no loan/benefit is being triggered under section 15 of the Income Tax Act. Larger injections exceeding CAD 1 million may trigger FINTRAC large-transaction reporting (CTR) and an ISED Investment Canada Act notification if the transaction constitutes acquisition of control of a Canadian business; for a de novo ULC funded by a US parent, only a routine OFSI/ISED confirmation is normally required, with no pre-approval barrier for amounts beneath the WTO-enterprise review threshold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational, trade, and intra-group disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 (priority SWIFT GPI) for cross-border USD/CAD payments, and Payments Canada Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or Real-Time Rail (RTR) for domestic CAD-clearing. For services and licensing fees to foreign contractors, an MT103 with purpose code 'SERVICES' or 'BUSINESS 2' is appropriate. The no-code builder's recurring global card revenue will be collected through Stripe Billing or Paddle using their respective payout rails into the ULC's Canadian operating account; commercial letters of credit (MT700) are only relevant if the ULC procures physical cloud infrastructure or enters equipment import contracts, in which case a confirmed irrevocable LC issued by RBC/TD via a Canadian bank branch and advised through a US or Asian correspondent is acceptable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX spot and outright forward contracts (up to 12–24 months tenor) executed with a Schedule I Canadian bank or a registered Canadian derivatives dealer; CAD is fully convertible, so no onshore NDF obligation arises.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps on intercompany loans (e.g., USD floating to CAD fixed) where the underlying is a documented intra-group borrowing under section 212.3 and transfer-pricing rules.

Vanilla FX options (European-style) for hedging forecasted SaaS subscription receipts and expected USD-CAD dividend remittances, provided the options are designated as hedging transactions under the ULC's tax-accrual methodology and supported by a board-approved treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 50 late-filing surcharge; failure to file for two consecutive years permits administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registrar of Companies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal corporate tax filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before six months after the end of the taxation year; December 31 year-end requires filing by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; daily compound interest at CRA prescribed rates; repeated-failure penalty of 10% for qualifying corporations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Treasury Board and Finance (administered and filed jointly with the federal T2 through CRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same due date as the federal T2: six months after the corporation's taxation year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and prescribed interest mirror the CRA T2 regime; unpaid Alberta corporate tax accrues daily compound interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (where annual filer status applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal or reporting year for annual GST/HST registrants
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 1% of net tax owing, plus daily compound interest at CRA prescribed rates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Summary and T4 Statements of Remuneration Paid (where employees exist)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February following the calendar year in which remuneration was paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties range from CAD 100 to CAD 2,500 per information return depending on the number of T4 slips; higher penalties for deliberate omissions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting or unanimous shareholder resolution waiving the AGM; minutes inserted in statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation and thereafter no more than 15 months after the previous AGM; waiver by unanimous shareholder resolution under the ABCA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government monetary penalty; non-compliance exposes directors to shareholder remedies (oppression remedy, derivative action) and may impair annual-return certification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under ABCA s. 151, a non-reporting private corporation (including an Alberta ULC) must appoint a public accountant (auditor) at each AGM unless all shareholders execute a unanimous resolution waiving the appointment for that fiscal year; no revenue or asset threshold makes an audit compulsory for a private ULC. A mandatory audit applies to a reporting issuer or distributing corporation under securities law (NI 52-102) or when shareholders holding at least 5% of the issued shares demand an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private Alberta ULC: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, CPA Canada Handbook Part II); publicly accountable or reporting ULC: IFRS (Part I). Statements are frequently prepared concurrently under US GAAP where a US parent consolidates the ULC as a disregarded entity for US tax purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: ABCA Part 15.1 requires an Alberta ULC to maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC/UBO register). The register must be updated within 15 days after the corporation becomes aware of any transfer or change in significant control. Annually, at the AGM or fiscal year-end, directors must reconfirm current shareholdings, voting rights, and beneficial ownership against the Register of Members and share-transfer records. Alberta does not currently require an annual public UBO filing for provincially incorporated ULCs; the register remains on site and must be produced to authorized persons on demand. Federal CBCA annual ISC reporting does not apply to provincial Alberta corporations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC/UBO register)
Register of All Transfers of Shares

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110-370 per annum (CAD 150-500) for a registered office or corporate agent service in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000-12,000 per annum for a small private ULC; avoidable for a given year if all shareholders sign the unanimous auditor-waiver resolution

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction (Alberta 2% on first CAD 500,000 for CCPC), SR&ED tax credit (35% refundable for CCPC on qualified expenditures), and investment tax credits for digital adoption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed via CRA's EFILE or NETFILE for corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after fiscal year-end (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, deadline is June 30 of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Canadian-source revenue only; allocate income per treaty rules.
Claim only expenses directly related to Canadian-source income; maintain supporting documentation.
Calculate based on Canadian GAAP/IFRS; adjust for tax-specific items.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (after adjustments and loss carryovers)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty provisions for permanent establishment and income allocation.
Compute using applicable rates; claim foreign tax credits if applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of balance owing plus 1% per month for up to 12 months (max 17%). Additional penalties for repeated failures and gross negligence (up to 50% of understated tax).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (reduced under applicable tax treaties, e.g., 15% for US residents under Canada-US treaty)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: File Form NR301 (for dividends) with CRA, attach Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority, and complete Form NR4 for each non-resident recipient. Treaty relief is applied at source if the payer has a valid TRC; otherwise, refund claim via T2 adjustment or Form NR7.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory, 15% under US-Canada treaty (for copyrights, patents, etc.); Interest: 25% statutory, 15% under US-Canada treaty (or 0% for arm's length interest on certain loans, e.g., long-term debt).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million for services, CAD 5 million for goods, CAD 10 million for intangibles (aggregate non-arm's length transactions with non-residents).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have ESR, but applies GAAR (General Anti-Avoidance Rule) and substance-over-form principles. A ULC must demonstrate real economic activity (e.g., employees, office, decision-making) to avoid recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or misrepresentation of Canadian-source revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% of understated tax (gross negligence), plus interest; criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act s.239 with fines up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax under s.227.1; civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment for willful evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: ULC with no real economic substance, used solely to shift profits or avoid Canadian tax (e.g., no employees, no office, no business activity).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment, denial of treaty benefits, and penalties up to 25% of tax avoided; possible criminal charges for tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes if they authorized or acquiesced in the sham arrangement; potential civil fraud claims and asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a Money Services Business (MSB) if processing payments for third parties, or failure to report suspicious transactions under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1 million for individuals and CAD 2 million for corporations; criminal penalties for money laundering up to 10 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for AML compliance failures if they knowingly or negligently fail to implement controls; travel bans and extradition possible for serious offenses.
